memory_update.text: SPSC is the cleanest mapped underfollowed Consumer infrastructure candidate in this chunk: retail supplier connectivity, EDI, trading-partner standards, recurring revenue, and potential operational switching costs.

DSGX should remain in the underfollowed lane as a logistics messaging, customs, cross-border compliance, and carrier-connectivity adjacency, but consumer-retail revenue materiality must be verified before elevation.

OTEX should be tracked as a hidden-segment Business Network / EDI candidate, but the segment may be too buried inside diversified enterprise software unless size, growth, and retail/CPG relevance are proven.

MANH is a reference retail operations software leader for WMS, OMS, and omnichannel workflows; it is useful for node validation but is less likely to be the hidden retail supplier-connectivity bottleneck.
BKNG is a reference travel marketplace benchmark only; Layer 1B expansion should search for smaller travel infrastructure companies one or two steps away from OTA demand aggregation.

For SPSC, verify primary-source metrics: recurring revenue percentage, customer count, net retention, gross retention, organic growth, acquisition contribution, revenue guidance, and tariff/macro commentary from filings and transcripts.
For DSGX, quantify revenue by product and end market: retail/ecommerce EDI, customs/compliance, transportation management, carrier network, global trade data, and general logistics software.

For OTEX, isolate OpenText Business Network: revenue size, organic growth, margin, retention, transaction volume, retail/CPG customer concentration, and whether the segment is material to consolidated valuation.

For MANH, determine whether supplier connectivity and EDI are monetized directly or only integrated through third-party networks; this determines whether MANH is a chokepoint or an adjacent workflow system.
For the travel lane, conduct a dedicated expansion beyond BKNG into hotel channel managers, PMS software, travel payments, fraud/identity, data, GDS, and niche lodging infrastructure.

summary: Layer 2B maps the candidate chunk into ticker-to-node relationships for a Consumer theme funnel. The strongest mapped cluster is retail supplier connectivity, EDI, trading-partner standards, logistics messaging, and retail operations software. SPSC is the highest-priority underfollowed relationship because the cached evidence and external context both point to a retail supply-chain network with recurring revenue, long operating history, retailer-specific integrations, and potential switching costs. DSGX and OTEX are underfollowed adjacent infrastructure mappings, but their exact consumer-retail materiality remains an evidence gap. MANH is a reference leader for retail operations and omnichannel execution rather than a hidden supplier-network pure play. BKNG is retained only as a reference travel marketplace benchmark so later work can look one or two steps away into smaller travel infrastructure companies. No buy, sell, target-price, or return recommendation is made.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify recurring revenue percentage, net revenue retention, gross retention, customer additions, ARPU, customer concentration, transaction-volume sensitivity, churn, acquisition contribution, and whether 2026 growth deceleration is cyclical supplier-spend deferral or saturation.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Pull latest SPSC 10-K, 10-Q, investor presentation, and earnings-call transcript; extract customer count, recurring revenue mix, retailer/supplier network size, retention metrics, organic growth, acquisition contribution, revenue guidance, and management commentary on tariff or macro-related supplier spend delays.
ticker_relationships.relationship: SPS Commerce maps most directly to the retail supplier connectivity node because it provides a retail supply-chain network connecting retailers, grocers, distributors, brands, 3PLs, carriers, and suppliers through EDI, order, fulfillment, and trading-partner workflows.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify how much of SPSC revenue and retention is driven by EDI compliance, retailer-specific mapping, ASN/routing-guide requirements, item-data synchronization, drop-ship workflows, and chargeback avoidance rather than broader software modules.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Review SPSC product pages, customer case studies, retailer partner documentation, contract language if available, and implementation guides to determine whether EDI mapping and retailer compliance are durable workflow bottlenecks.
ticker_relationships.relationship: SPSC appears to sit at the EDI and trading-partner standards layer by maintaining retailer-specific EDI maps, compliance logic, onboarding workflows, and connections among suppliers and major retailers.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Determine whether SPSC revenue is more correlated with supplier count, retail integration complexity, and recurring subscriptions than with volatile retail GMV or consumer discretionary demand.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Compare SPSC historical revenue growth through retail cycles against retail sales, ecommerce growth, customer additions, and acquisition-adjusted organic revenue growth.
ticker_relationships.relationship: SPSC is a second-order Consumer infrastructure candidate because it monetizes the operational complexity behind retail replenishment and supplier compliance rather than direct consumer sell-through.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Determine how much revenue comes from retail/supplier EDI, ecommerce, customs, transportation management, network transaction fees, and recurring SaaS versus unrelated logistics software modules.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Pull DSGX annual report, MD&A, investor deck, segment disclosures, acquisition history, and product taxonomy; map revenue and product modules to retail, ecommerce, customs, transportation management, and logistics-network usage.
ticker_relationships.relationship: Descartes maps to logistics messaging and carrier connectivity as a broader logistics technology and B2B connectivity network that can support transportation, shipment visibility, customs, ecommerce, and trading-partner workflows.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify whether DSGX has material customs, denied-party screening, global trade intelligence, import/export filing, or country-of-origin compliance revenue tied to retail and ecommerce customers.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Review DSGX product pages and filings for customs/compliance products, customer examples in retail/ecommerce, and management commentary on trade policy, tariffs, customs complexity, or cross-border ecommerce demand.
ticker_relationships.relationship: Descartes may benefit from cross-border commerce compliance if tariff volatility, customs enforcement, sanctions screening, and country-of-origin documentation increase the value of global trade data and logistics compliance tools.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Separate retail supplier EDI and trading-partner connectivity from freight forwarding, carrier, customs broker, and general logistics software exposure.
